Kibble.Logging.EventSchema module¶

Kibble.Logging.EventSchema.LatencyStructure(status_data: dict, severity: LogLevel = LogLevel.CRITICAL, device_id: bson.ObjectId | None = None, monitor_id: int | None = None) → dict¶

Builds an LatencyStructure endpoint-status event document for logging latency based telemetry.

Parameters:

  • status_data – Dict with “alive”, “latency”, and “last_updated” status.

  • severity – Log level (default CRITICAL).

  • device_id – Required device ObjectId; must not be None.

  • monitor_id – Integer ID of the monitoring node that produced this event.

Returns:

Event dict with schema_version, timestamp, event_type, status, severity_level, device_id, and monitor_id.

Raises:

ValueError – If device_id is None.

Kibble.Logging.EventSchema.TelemetryStructure(status_data: dict, device_id: bson.ObjectId, severity: LogLevel = LogLevel.CRITICAL, monitor_id: int | None = None) → dict¶

Builds a TelemetryStrcuture endpoint-status event document for logging daemon based telemetry.

Parameters:

  • status_dict – dict with “alive”, “latency”, “last_updated”, and “telemetry”.

  • severity – Log level

  • device_id – the Device ObjectId

  • monitor_id – Integer ID of the monitoring node that produced this event.

Returns:

dict with schema_version, timestamp, even_type, status, severity_level, and device_id

Kibble.Logging.EventSchema.device_configuration(device_id: bson.ObjectId, interfaces: list[bson.ObjectId], applied_date: datetime) → dict¶

Builds a device-configuration snapshot: which interface rows apply at applied_date.

Parameters:

  • device_id – Device ObjectId; required.

  • interfaces – Interface document ObjectIds (non-empty after inserts).

  • applied_date – When this snapshot was observed or applied (timezone-aware recommended).

Returns:

Dict with schema_version, device_id, interfaces, applied_date.

Raises:

ValueError – If device_id is None or interfaces is empty.

Kibble.Logging.EventSchema.device_info(device_type_id: bson.ObjectId | None, endpoint_ip: str, status_data: dict) → dict¶

Builds a device-info document from endpoint IP and status data.

Parameters:

  • device_type_id – Device type ObjectId; required.

  • asset_tag – Integer asset tag; should be unique per device (sparse unique index recommended).

Returns:

Dict with asset_tag and device_type_id.

Raises:

ValueError – If device_type_id is None.

Kibble.Logging.EventSchema.device_types(name: str, protocols_supported: list[str])¶

Builds a device-type document with name and supported protocols.

Parameters:

  • name – Display name of the device type.

  • protocols_supported – List of protocol identifiers (e.g. “ICMP”); copied into the doc.

Returns:

Dict with “name” and “protocols_supported”.

Kibble.Logging.EventSchema.interface_configuration(device_id: bson.ObjectId, interface_name: str, ip_address: str, subnet_mask: str, default_gateway: str, hostname: str, mac_address: str, applied_date: datetime) → dict¶

Builds an interface-configuration document for a device.

Parameters:

  • device_id – Owning device _id.

  • interface_name – Interface key (e.g. "default" for the primary row from scans).

  • ip_address – Current IPv4/IPv6 address (may be empty when only hostname is known).

  • subnet_mask – Subnet mask for the interface.

  • default_gateway – Default gateway for this interface.

  • hostname – Resolved or configured hostname.

  • mac_address – Interface MAC address.

  • applied_date – When this snapshot was observed (used for history and IP->device resolution).

Returns:

Dict with schema_version, device_id, interface fields, and applied_date.
